prompt: Which producers are the foundation on which all other businesses depend?
explanation: Raw goods. Raw-goods producers provide goods in their natural, or raw, state. These producers are the foundation on which all other businesses depend. They include such businesses as farming, mining, fisheries, and lumber companies. A manufacturer is a type of producer that changes the shapes, or forms, of materials so that they will be useful to consumers. A builder is a type of producer that constructs roads, bridges, buildings, or houses. A retailer is a business that buys consumer goods or services and sells them to the ultimate consumer.

prompt: A computer-chip manufacturer sells its product line to computer manufacturers such as Compaq. This is often referred to as __________ selling.
explanation: Business-to-business. When the purpose of the sale is to purchase the product (e.g., chip) for business purposes or for resale to a retailer at a profit, it is considered business-to-business selling. The chip manufacturer, which is a business, is selling the chip to another business, which makes computers. Distributors are defined as businesses or individuals who make goods available for sale by getting them from the producer to the retailer or customer. Wholesalers are intermediaries who buy goods from producers or agents and sell them to retailers. Retailers sell products to the end user or consumer, not to the wholesaler or distributor.

prompt: Making both buyers and sellers feel they are getting good value is part of the __________ function of marketing.
explanation: Pricing. Pricing determines and adjusts what customers pay for products to maximize returns and meet customers' perceptions of value. Prices must be set so that both buyers and sellers feel that they are getting the most value. Purchasing is the planning and procedures necessary to obtain goods and services for use in the operation of a business. Promotion is the communication of information about goods, services, images, and/or ideas to achieve a desired outcome. Financing involves understanding the financial concepts used in making business decisions.

prompt: What activity is part of the industrial purchasing process?
explanation: Identifying sources of supply. Industrial purchasing involves locating and selecting potential sources of supply. These sources must be able to provide items that meet the business's required characteristics and specifications. Industrial purchasers should then obtain price and delivery quotations from potential suppliers. Identifying suppliers that can deliver the needed goods or services on time and at acceptable prices is an important part of the industrial purchasing process. The industrial purchasing process does not involve arranging demonstrations of goods, determining availability of funds, or analyzing needs of the sales staff.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of an expense that a technical business would include in the operating expenses category of a profit-and-loss statement:
explanation: Insurance payments. The operating expenses category of a profit-and-loss statement includes all the expenses incurred from keeping a technical business's doors open. Some examples include insurance payments (premiums), wages, salaries, utilities, and rent. The technical business pays these expenses in order to operate. The operating expenses category does not cover the cost of goods sold, which includes such expenses as shipping charges to obtain goods for resale, cost of raw materials to produce goods, and items returned by customers.

prompt: One way that a technical equipment company protects its vital records is by
choices: keeping them in the business office.
storing them in a safe environment.
explanation: Storing them in a safe environment. Records need to be maintained in a safe physical environment in order to protect them from damage or destruction. Technical equipment companies often protect their records by storing them in fireproof safes, fire-resistant cabinets, or moisture-controlled rooms. Because technology is constantly evolving, many people believe that videotapes are outdated, if not obsolete. Insufficient information is provided to determine whether the business office offers a safe environment. In addition, vital records may be kept in areas other than the business office. Filing records in cardboard boxes is not safe because cardboard boxes may be destroyed by fire or water.

prompt: Lois and Lora plan to open a computer repair business. Lois is unable to devote full time to the daily operations of the business, but wishes to provide financial support. Which form of business partnership is most likely to appeal to Lois?
explanation: Limited. Limited partnership permits a partner to invest in a computer repair business, but limits responsibility. A general partnership is one in which all partners are liable for the business's losses. Close refers to a corporation that is owned by a few people and does not offer its shares for sale to the general public. A nonprofit corporation is a business that has a specific mission or purpose other than to make a profit. Many times, the mission or purpose of the organization is to help society. Any income made by a nonprofit organization is used to cover expenses.

prompt: What challenges do technical sales representatives face since technology is changing at increasingly rapid rates?
choices: Most of the sales representatives have seen increases in their required sales calls and quotas.
Sales representatives must find ways to present more new products to their customers very quickly.
Sales representatives are generally not receiving training in selling techniques and customer service.
More government regulations and higher sales taxes on technical products have lowered representatives' bonuses.
explanation: Sales representatives must find ways to present more new products to their customers very quickly. Because technology is advancing at very rapid rates, new products are also available at more rapid rates. These advancements have also created higher competition among technical product companies to get newer, improved technical products to the marketplace in a quick and efficient manner. Therefore, technical companies feel pressure to develop ways to get all these new products to the consumers faster than their competitors do. Although some sales representatives have seen increases in their sales calls and quotas, not all of them have. Some technical businesses might revise their payment structure due to government regulation changes, but this does not always happen. In addition, bonuses are based on company policies, so sales taxes do not necessarily lower a technical sales representative's bonus.

prompt: Jeff is a stock clerk in an electronics store, and his friend Eric is a server in a restaurant. Which of the following statements is true about their safety at work:
choices: They are exposed to the same safety hazards.
They are exposed to different safety hazards.
Jeff's job has more safety hazards than Eric's.
Jeff's job has fewer safety hazards than Eric's.
explanation: They are exposed to different safety hazards. The types of safety hazards employees encounter depends upon where people work and the type of work that they do. The number of hazards each faces depends upon many factors, such as employees' observance of safety rules, management's attention to unsafe conditions, and the business's enforcement of safety regulations.

prompt: The Age Discrimination in Employment Act prohibits employment discrimination because of age against people who are __________ or older.
explanation: 40. The Age Discrimination in Employment Act was first passed in 1967 and amended in 1986. It prohibits employers from discriminating against people who are 40 or older. One of the main provisions of the act prevents businesses from firing older employees simply because of their age.

prompt: Sales tax, which consumers are required to pay in addition to the cost of electronic merchandise, may be recorded and reported
choices: several years after it is collected.
explanation: Automatically by POS functions. Electronics retailers are required to collect sales tax from consumers, which is over and above the purchase price of the merchandise. Electronics retailers must also record and report to the federal government the sales tax they collect. This can be done fairly easily today with the electronics retailers' automated POS (point-of-sale) terminals, which are capable of collecting and reporting a variety of customer, sales, and financial information. Each salesperson does not record and report sales tax information. POS software enables this information to be batched from all terminals, resulting in one consolidated report. IRS auditors do not record and report sales tax information as part of their regular functions. If auditing an electronics retailer, they would be looking at the retailer's income and expenses, deductions, etc. Sales tax must be reported on a regular basis, usually quarterly, by electronics retailers, according to rules provided by the federal government. It cannot be recorded and reported several years after it is collected.

prompt: When an employee realizes that a caller needs to speak to some other employee or department, the person should
choices: take notes to pass on to the appropriate person or department.
ask the caller to call back for the appropriate person.
put the caller on hold, and transfer the call.
give the caller the correct number, and transfer the call.
explanation: Give the caller the correct number, and transfer the call. When you need to transfer calls, it is good practice to explain the reason for the transfer to callers, give them the number to which they are being transferred, and then make the transfer. This is more effective than putting callers on hold and transferring calls. If the line is busy, or the transfer is not completed for some reason, callers will have the correct extension number when they want to call back. Asking callers to make another call now indicates a lack of good service. Taking notes is unnecessary since the caller's business will be handled by someone else.

prompt: What type of simple report might a buyer for an electronic parts distributor prepare in order to periodically inform other departments about the status of scheduled deliveries?
explanation: Progress. A progress report is a type of simple report that an electronic parts distributor might use to keep the various departments informed of business activities. Progress reports briefly provide updated information about long-term activities. They are short and usually include only summaries of necessary information. Analytical, research, and statistical are examples of complex written reports that are lengthy and contain detailed information.

prompt: What type of information is often transmitted through upward communication?
explanation: Suggestions. Upward communication involves sending a message to someone at a higher level in the business. Many businesses encourage upward communication by making it possible for employees to send suggestions and comments to management. Employees who have suggestions on how to improve quality or make positive changes are given an opportunity to transmit that information upward to managers. Instructions, evaluations, and corrections are usually transmitted from a higher level down to employees at a lower level.

prompt: Which of the following would probably use a longer channel of distribution than the others:
explanation: A bottle of shampoo. Shampoo is a low-cost, standard product that would probably use a longer channel of distribution than the other alternatives. Baby ducks are perishable and need to use short channels. A printing press is highly technical, requires installation, and is quite heavy; therefore, it would rely on short channels. An airplane is technical and quite heavy and would probably use a direct route from the producer to the industrial user.

prompt: Information technology has dramatically improved supply-chain management capability by creating a seamless distribution process for matching
explanation: Inventory needs to customer requirements. The heart of physical distribution is timeliness, availability, and quality. Improved information technology has made customer product information readily available, allowing for a more efficient distribution process. Matching costs with expense information is more often handled in finance management. Production innovation is not considered part of the distribution process. Distribution centers are tied to inventory needs in the distribution process and the path a product may take on its way to the consumer.

prompt: Electronics businesses that sell gray-market goods often charge discounted prices that may have a negative effect on
explanation: Authorized dealers. Gray-market goods are foreign-made products that are imported into countries by suppliers that are not authorized by the manufacturers. The distributors of gray-market goods bypass the authorized distribution channels that enables them to sell the goods at low prices. Electronics businesses that buy gray-market goods for resale often charge discounted prices. This practice has a negative effect on authorized dealers that purchased the same goods from the manufacturers and are not able to offer large discounts. Customers benefit because they are able to buy products at low prices. Exporters sell goods and services to businesses in other countries. A carrier is a transportation company such as a railroad, airline, or trucking company.

prompt: Elentra Electronics is preparing invoices for its retail customers. One customer ordered 35 digital cameras priced at $467.49 each and 42 camera cases priced at $27.99 each. What is the gross amount that is reflected on the customer's invoice?
explanation: $17,537.73. An invoice, or bill, is a printed or written document that indicates the total amount due for an order. Generally, businesses send invoices to customers after the order has shipped. The extension on the invoice is determined by multiplying the quantity of an ordered item by the unit price of the item. The gross amount is determined by adding all the extensions together. The gross amount of an invoice reflects the total amount due before discounts. Computation is as follows: $467.49 x 35 = $16,362.15; $27.99 x 42 = $ 1,175.58; $16,362.15 + $1,175.58 = $17,537.73.

prompt: Providing quality customer service is one reason why technical businesses often coordinate distribution with other
explanation: Marketing activities. Distribution is one of the marketing functions that must work with the other marketing activities to get goods and services from producers to consumers. The goal of marketing is to satisfy consumer wants and needs while achieving company goals. Technical businesses cannot satisfy those needs and provide quality customer service unless all the marketing activities work together. For example, technical businesses are only able to serve customers when they have the advertised items on hand and at the right price. Business objectives are the goals that a technical company wants to reach. Operating techniques are the ways that a technical business functions on a daily basis. Staffing procedures involve finding workers for the technical business.

prompt: When a business makes a product that requires considerable technical and market information to sell and the business does not want to maintain a sales force, the business often employs a(n) __________ as a channel member.
explanation: Manufacturer's agent. These channel members work as independent businesspeople who sell the products of several producers. They use their market connections and technical knowledge to sell products on a commission basis. The producer pays the agent based on merchandise sold and does not have to maintain a sales force. Industrial distributors often stock competitors' brands and cannot be relied on to sell a particular producer's products aggressively. Retailers and wholesalers tend to work with the consumer rather than industrial markets.

prompt: Which of the following is most likely to add form utility to a good:
explanation: Producer. Producers are the growers, providers, or manufacturers of goods and services. Producers create form utility by altering or changing the shape or form of a product to make it more useful to consumers. Retailers, agents, and other marketers are not directly responsible for creating form utility.

prompt: When changes in a product's price cause corresponding changes in consumer demand, the product has
explanation: Elastic demand. The nature of a product determines its elasticity. Consumers continue to buy a necessity, such as milk, even when its price increases. Milk, therefore, has fairly inelastic demand, whereas a nonessential product, such as a boat, has elastic demand. Product utility is the perceived usefulness of a good or service to consumers.

prompt: An example of a government using price supports is when the government
choices: sells the electricity produced by a government-owned facility to consumers.
buys supplies from businesses for its workers to use.
employs thousands of workers across the country.
buys wheat to keep the price high enough for farmers to make a profit.
explanation: Buys wheat to keep the price high enough for farmers to make a profit. Price supports are assistance by the government to maintain the price of a good or service in order to enable the producers to earn a profit. Buying supplies from businesses for its workers to use, employing thousands of workers across the country, and selling electricity produced by a government-owned facility to consumers are examples of ways that a government has assumed a more active role in the world of business.

prompt: The first major federal law (1890) that was passed to encourage competition in business was the __________ Act.
explanation: Sherman. The Sherman Antitrust Act of 1890 was passed to encourage competition and prohibit most monopolies. The Clayton Act (1914), the Robinson-Patman Act (1936), and the Wheeler-Lea Act (1938) further defined the original plan to protect consumers by adding protection from unfair and deceptive advertising, competition, and pricing.

prompt: There are 634,820 people in the labor force in a large metropolitan area. If 34,290 are currently out of work, what is the rate of unemployment?
explanation: 5.4%. The unemployment rate is the percentage of those unemployed people in the labor force who are actively looking for work. To calculate the rate of unemployment, divide the number of unemployed by the number in the labor force (34,290 ÷ 634,820 = .0540 or 5.4%). The rate of unemployment is used to analyze the condition of the economy. A low unemployment rate indicates a healthy economy because most of the people who want to work are working. However, a high unemployment rate indicates a slowdown in the economy because more people are out of work.

prompt: One of the main benefits of trade between nations is __________ goods and services.
explanation: A better variety of. There are many benefits of trade between nations. One of the main benefits is a better variety of goods and services because several nations are selling their goods and services to each other. Trade between nations does not create higher prices for goods and services, decrease sales of goods and services, or lower the quantity of goods and services.

prompt: A computer software company that is conducting a survey to determine its customers' preferences and satisfaction levels is gathering__________ information.
explanation: Marketing. Marketing information is all the marketing-related data available from inside and outside the computer software company. Surveying customers to determine their preferences is one way of gathering primary, external information about the market that the computer software company is trying to serve. Internal information is obtained from sources found within the computer software company and includes operating information (e.g., production reports, budgets). Secondary information is data that has been collected for purposes other than the project at hand.

prompt: Marketing research can affect a cellular phone company's marketing mix by providing information about available goods, services, and ideas that will influence the company's __________ decision.
explanation: Product. The product decision involves selecting the goods, services, or ideas that a cellular phone company will sell. Marketing research can provide a cellular phone company with information about what is available, how it is selling, who sells it, etc. The place decision involves getting products in the right place at the right time. The price decision involves determining the amount of money that a cellular phone company will ask in exchange for its products. The promotion decision involves deciding which of the various types of communications that a cellular phone company will use to inform, persuade, or remind customers of the company and its products.

prompt: What is the measurement of central tendency that indicates the exact middle?
explanation: Median. The median is the middle value. That means that the number above the median is the same as the number below the median. For example, if 60 people respond to a questionnaire and 20 answer "A," 20 answer "B," and 20 answer "C," the median is "B" because there is an equal number higher and lower. The mode is the response most often given to a question. The mean is the arithmetic average of all the responses in a sample. Model is not a measurement of central tendency.

prompt: Which of the following is least likely to necessitate a change in marketing strategies:
choices: Increases in the cost of production
explanation: Increases in company profits. Increased profits would indicate that the company's marketing strategies are successful and not currently in need of change. Factors that may prompt a business to change marketing strategies include the actions of competitors and suppliers, increases in the cost of production, the influences of governmental agencies, and changes in consumer attitudes. Marketing strategies should be designed so that they are flexible enough to accommodate changes as needed.

prompt: Today's customers are not influenced by mass marketing alone because they are more
explanation: Discerning. Today's customers may be more decisive, determined, or disciplined, but it is their increased discernment that is related to the fact that they are not influenced by mass marketing alone.

prompt: Technical businesses most frequently use geodemographic information in marketing its products when consumer
explanation: Tastes differ by region. Geodemographic information combines geographic data with census data to allow technical businesses to differentiate consumers by their regions and by their preferences. This information helps technical businesses determine the fastest growing areas. Age is a demographic factor. Consumers' interests are psychographic data and customer value is part of benefit segmentation.

prompt: Deciding how to allocate funds and when to purchase additional materials and equipment are ways that most technical businesses use their
explanation: Sales forecasts. Sales forecasts are predictions of what a firm's sales will be during a specific future time period using a certain marketing plan. Many technical businesses say that the sales forecast is the cornerstone of their planning and use it as the basis for making a wide variety of decisions. Sales forecasts help a technical business decide how to allocate funds by indicating what the company's cash flow is expected to be. Sales forecasts tell a technical business what amounts of materials and equipment it will need to produce the products it expects to sell. Personal budgets are the budgets of individuals. Credit policies are guidelines for businesses to follow in controlling the use of payment plans that allow customers to purchase now and pay later. Financial quotas are quotas that attempt to relate sales to an organization's total expenses or profits.

prompt: One reason why UltraTech Computer Parts conducts an annual review of the marketing plan is to
choices: set the stage for long-term market planning.
explanation: Set the stage for long-term market planning. Technical businesses, such as UltraTech Computer Parts, review their marketing plans to do long-term planning, which may result in expansion or diversification. Technical businesses do not review marketing plans to check for mistakes, meet federal standards, or share information with employees.

prompt: Jim believes that he is better than his coworkers because he has had some college classes and they have not. Jim's coworkers dislike his __________ attitude.
explanation: Superior. Conceited, arrogant, and snobbish are other terms frequently used to describe people with a superior attitude toward others. Such immature people frequently try to dominate others when they are in a group setting. People with a positive attitude look on the bright side of things. Aggressive people ignore the rights of and exploit others in order to achieve personal goals.

prompt: Computer World's front-end employees are trained to smile and greet customers as they approach the checkstand and say thank-you as customers leave. This approach
explanation: Builds customer loyalty. Employee courtesy at the checkstand reminds customers that Computer World appreciates their business, which builds customer loyalty to the store. Employee courtesy should not encourage rivalry among front-end employees. Building customer loyalty through courtesy would increase, not decrease, customer patronage. A decrease in employee productivity should not occur as the result of courtesy toward customers.

prompt: Jonathan works in his small town's only video store. He is on a first-name basis with most of the customers who come in. Cheryl is a difficult customer. Sometimes she's really friendly, and other times she snaps at Jonathan. She is a(n) __________ customer.
explanation: Irritable/Moody. Cheryl is an irritable/moody customer. Sometimes, she is Jonathan's best friend, and other times, she's a real crab. A suspicious customer questions everything and is constantly worried that the business might take advantage of him/her. A slow/methodical customer is indecisive or just takes a long time to make up his or her mind. A dishonest customer may try to steal or get a discount on merchandise that isn't on sale.

prompt: The Conrad Computer Company needs to hire another warehouse worker. The warehouse manager wants to include the phrase, "requires heavy lifting" in the employment ad. It is ethical to use this phrase only when the job
choices: would be better performed by males.
would be better performed by females.
explanation: Actually requires heavy lifting. A job announcement should clearly communicate the requirements needed to be successful and encourage qualified people to apply. If it is used to discourage certain groups from applying, the announcement is unethical. For example, it is unethical to include such a phrase if the intention is to prevent either men or women from applying. The phrase is deceptive if the job does not require heavy lifting.

prompt: Which of the following suggestions can help you present the content of a job orientation in a logical, easy-to-follow format:
choices: Giving detailed information in small doses
Discussing each point of a presentation thoroughly before moving to the next
Using appropriate follow-up strategies after a job-orientation program
explanation: Discussing each point of a presentation thoroughly before moving to the next. Your goal is to make it easy for new employees to learn and to remember the information presented. Giving detailed information in small doses helps to avoid confusing and/or frustrating listeners by enabling them to absorb more information. By encouraging questions, you can learn how much of your presentation has been understood and what points need clarification and elaboration. Follow-up strategies do not affect logical presentation of materials.

prompt: Why is it important for the Comput-A-Chip Manufacturing Company to provide training and development activities for its managers/supervisors?
choices: Their work affects the business's success.
Their jobs lack interest and variety.
explanation: Their work affects the business's success. The training and development that managers/supervisors receive should help them to acquire the knowledge, skills, and attitudes needed to manage the performance of other employees in achieving the organization's goals. Because of the impact that managers and supervisors have on other workers, their performance is vital to the Comput-A-Chip Manufacturing Company's success. Not all managers or supervisors need to be challenged or want to be promoted. Most managerial/supervisory jobs are both interesting and varied.

prompt: Which of the following is a way that the electronics store employees who handle sales transactions can help the store save money:
explanation: Watching for counterfeit money. Electronics store employees who handle sales transactions have excellent opportunities to save money for the business. They can do this by watching for counterfeit money. An employee who accepts counterfeit money actually costs a business money because the counterfeit currency is worthless. In effect, the business has given away a good or service free of charge. Most businesses do not accept third-party checks. Employees should always validate credit cards and count out the exact amount of change.

prompt: In which of the following situations might a computer software company pay more than the normal rate to purchase a service contract on large pieces of equipment:
choices: Fee includes cost of house calls.
Business pays on a monthly basis.
explanation: Fee includes cost of house calls. A business such as a computer software company might negotiate service contracts that include house calls, because it is impossible to disassemble and move large pieces of equipment. The house-call option might cost the computer software company as much as 30% to 50% more than a contract without this feature. Despite the expense, the house-call option is important to computer software companies that have large pieces of equipment that cannot be moved. The replacement price is not a factor in the cost of a service contract. Long-term contracts usually are less expensive than short-term contracts. Many computer software companies pay for service on a monthly basis.

prompt: The information in an operating budget usually is presented in which of the following forms:
explanation: Dollar. The information in an operating budget usually is presented in the numerical form of dollars. Stating the estimated dollar amount of revenue and expenses is the basis of most budgets. Seeing these figures in dollar form helps the business develop financial plans and allocate funds. Percent indicates how big a part of the whole amount one part is. Ratio is a mathematical expression of the comparison between two factors. A fraction is each of the mathematical units created when a whole number is broken down or separated into two or more equal parts.

prompt: A technical business's budget estimated $165,500 in sales each month for the next four months with 55% of that amount each month for expenses. If actual sales for the four-month period were $690,000 and expenses stayed at 55%, by what amount did the technical business's income increase?
explanation: $12,600. Technical businesses use budget information to monitor sales and expenses and to compare budgeted amounts with actual figures. If sales increase over the amount budgeted and expenses remain steady, the technical business's income will also increase. In this example, the technical business's actual sales increased over the budgeted amount. To calculate the increase in income, first determine the budgeted four-month sales total ($165,500 x 4 = $662,000). Then, calculate the amount of that figure that was budgeted for expenses ($662,000 x 55% or .55 = $364,100). Then, subtract budgeted expenses from budgeted sales to calculate budgeted income ($662,000 - $364,100 = $297,900). Next, calculate the amount of expenses based on actual sales ($690,000 x 55% or .55 = $379,500). Subtract expenses from actual sales to calculate actual income ($690,000 - $379,500 = $310,500). To determine the increase in income, subtract budgeted income from actual income ($310,500 - $297,900 = $12,600).

prompt: After analyzing its cash flow pattern, what action could a computer store take to increase the flow of cash into the business?
explanation: Revise credit terms. Credit terms are the time limits a computer store sets for its customers to pay for goods and services. Credit terms often have an effect on the computer store's cash flow because they may be too lenient and allow customers a long time to pay. The computer store will experience cash flow problems if its customers do not pay in a timely manner. The computer store should analyze its cash flow patterns and revise its credit terms in order to make sure that money is coming in when needed. One way to improve cash flow is to offer trade discounts to encourage customers to pay promptly. Buying more inventory and offering extended payment often reduce cash flow.

prompt: Which of the following is a false statement about competition:
choices: Technical businesses compete on a number of bases.
Price is the best basis for competition.
A carefully planned marketing program can be damaged by a competitor's actions.
Technical businesses should study their competitors' strengths, weaknesses, and mistakes.
explanation: Price is the best basis for competition. There is no one basis for competition that is considered best for all technical businesses. Price is only one basis. Other bases for competition include product quality, features, and availability. All of the other alternatives are true statements about competition.

prompt: A trait that people employed in technical selling often need in order to be successful is the ability to
explanation: Build relationships. The ability to build relationships is important to people who are employed in technical selling. Technical selling often involves selling expensive products to large corporations or specialized industries. Salespeople in this area usually need to develop relationships with those customers in order to build trust and obtain long-term commitments. A strong relationship makes customers feel that they are important and can depend on the salespeople to solve problems. Successful salespeople are assertive rather than aggressive, do not pressure customers, and they behave ethically.

prompt: Lynne discovered that the accounting courses she needed to take in order to get a new job were not easy, but she worked hard and passed the courses. What characteristic was Lynne exhibiting?
explanation: Perseverance. Perseverance is the ability to keep at something until it is finished. It is very important to achieving goals. Honesty is truthfulness. Assertiveness is the ability to stand up for yourself without trampling the rights of others. Independence is the ability to act on your own without assistance.

prompt: Cellular phone businesses often consider an employee's knowledge of the job, abilities, and skills when deciding whether to __________ the employee.
explanation: Promote. An employee who understands the job and has the appropriate abilities and skills is often considered for promotion. Many cellular phone businesses prefer to promote from within and review an employee's performance in order to make a decision. Employees who develop and improve their skills and abilities often move up the career ladder and are rewarded with promotions and additional responsibilities. A good evaluation might lead to an interview for a more important position and a promotion. Cellular phone businesses counsel employees when they are not performing as expected.

prompt: An employee who wants to stay current regarding the trends and technological advancements in the digital imaging industry might consider
choices: taking a management and leadership seminar.
subscribing to a general electronics publication.
developing a web-based newsletter for industry leaders.
explanation: Joining a national trade association. Trade associations are organizations that consist of members with similar or common goals, usually work or career related. By joining a trade association, an employee gets up-to-date information pertaining to the digital imaging industry. Information might include trends, processes, innovations, and developments in inks and presses and other professional-development opportunities such as seminars, trade shows, and potential employer contacts. While subscribing to a general electronics publication or taking a management and leadership seminar can provide opportunities for personal and professional growth, they are not specifically oriented or geared to the digital imaging industry. Developing a web-based newsletter does not aid an employee in keeping current on trends and developments.

prompt: A high promotional budget increases the price of technical goods because an electronics manufacturer includes that amount of money in the
explanation: Cost of the product. Most electronics manufacturers have promotional budgets. The amount of money spent on an advertising campaign is built into the cost of the technical products, which is the total amount of money spent to manufacture the technical goods. Therefore, the higher the promotional budget, the higher the price of the technical goods. Operating expenses are all of the expenditures necessary to keep the electronics manufacturer running. The salaries of management are included in operating expenses. Capital investment is the funds the electronics manufacturer has reinvested in the business.

prompt: Which of the following is a system developed by advances in technology that many electronics retailers use to read prices on products:
explanation: Optical scanning. Optical scanning is a method of reading prices that are marked electronically. These prices usually are encoded in bar codes that are printed on products. The scanners are able to quickly read the prices and process the information for checkout. One of the benefits of optical scanning is that it allows customers to scan their purchases and complete the checkout process without assistance from employees. As a result, many electronics retailers may be able to reduce the number of employees needed to read prices and manually ring up purchases. Digital surveying, global positioning, and interactive processing are not systems that electronics retailers use to read prices on products.

prompt: Cellular phone manufacturers that price their goods and services at the same level as those charged by other comparable businesses are setting prices based on
explanation: Industry standards. The industry in which a business operates helps to determine a company's pricing objectives. Cellular phone manufacturers consider their competition's pricing for comparable products when setting their own prices. Product life cycle refers to the stages through which products move from the time they are introduced on the market until they are taken off the market. A target market is the particular group of customers that a business seeks to attract. Channel members are the businesses or individuals who assist in moving goods and services from the producer to the consumer. Cellular phone manufacturers that price their goods and services at the same level as those charged by other comparable businesses are not setting prices based on product life cycles, channel members, or target markets.

prompt: During which stage of the product life cycle do technical companies spend most of their money trying to fend off the competition?
explanation: Maturity. During this stage, the technical product has asserted itself in the market and attracted competitors who wish to take away or gain back market share. In the introductory stage, advertising is focused on awareness. During the growth stage, advertising is focused on consumer satisfaction. During the decline stage, advertising may cease completely.

prompt: Satellite communications systems often impact the product/service management function by helping electronics distributors to
explanation: Track shipments. An important part of product/service management involves maintaining and improving the good or service because customers expect a quality good or service that keeps up with advances in technology. Satellite communications systems make it possible for electronics distributors to track shipments for customers, thereby improving the good or service. If an electronics distributor sells a product, it can track the product from the time it is ordered until it is delivered. If the electronics distributor sells a service such as delivery, it can use satellite communications systems to track the delivery process. Satellite communications systems do not help to order replacements, evaluate information, or use software.

prompt: An computer software engineer comes up with an idea to fix a problem with a new software program while driving home from work. This is an example of
explanation: Unconscious problem solving. Unconscious problem solving involves idea generation by relaxation and distraction from the problem, situation, or issue. In the example, the computer software engineer comes up with an idea while focused on something else—driving a vehicle. Subconscious decision making, subliminal message generation, and deliberate mind mapping are not terms commonly used to describe a creative-thinking technique that generates ideas in a relaxed or distracted state of mind.

prompt: Two characteristics of a good guarantee are that it should be
explanation: Unconditional and understandable. A good guarantee should be unconditional. In other words, there should be no conditions that the customer must meet in order for the guarantee to be in effect. It should be understandable. The language should be clear and the promises specific. The customer should not have to fill out a great many forms, see several different people, or travel to different locations in order to obtain satisfaction. It should be easy for the customer to implement and to collect. Whenever possible, the customer's money should be refunded on the spot.

prompt: Which of the following is a reason that a electronics manufacturer would make changes to its products:
choices: To predict the success of the changed product
To spread risk over a wider area
To keep up with changing consumer preferences
To make room for other products
explanation: To keep up with changing consumer preferences. Consumers' attitudes toward products change over time, and their preference for a product may change. Altering the product in some way can renew customers' interest. Making room for other products is a reason for using the contraction strategy. By adding products to the product mix, an electronics manufacturer is able to spread risk over a wider area. A limitation to the alteration strategy is that the electronics manufacturer cannot predict the success of altered products.

prompt: Encouraging customers to buy products that they might not otherwise want to buy is one reason why some software companies __________ products.
explanation: Bundle. Product bundling involves combining several products and selling them for one all-inclusive price. Software companies often bundle products to encourage customers to buy products that they might not otherwise want to buy. The price of the bundled products is usually lower than the combined price of the products sold separately. The lower price is an incentive to buy. As a result, customers buy the total package which may include products that they ordinarily would not purchase. Software companies routinely promote, market, and display products. However, these activities usually are not very effective in encouraging customers to buy products that they do not want.

prompt: Reasons for removing a specific technical product from a company's technical product line include all of the following except
choices: to replace with a new product.
to avoid conflict with other products in the line.
explanation: To appeal to new markets. To appeal to new markets is a reason for expanding the product line rather than contracting the product line. Product obsolescence, replacing a product with another, and removing a technical product because of conflict between other products in the line are all dominant reasons for contracting a technical product line.

prompt: By deciding whether a brand will be a manufacturer's brand or a private brand, a digital camera company is deciding who will ____________ the brand.
explanation: Sponsor. The manufacturer can sponsor the brand and sell it as a manufacturer's brand. Or, the manufacturer can turn the product over to an intermediary who sponsors the brand and sells it as a private brand. In either case, it is consumers rather than sellers who decide whether they will accept the brand, prefer it to other brands, and purchase it.

prompt: Customers appreciate services such as having their computers repaired at home, because it
choices: allows the computer technician plenty of time to work.
saves customers both time and effort.
reduces the number of repairs that the technician must make.
lets the computer technician test the equipment.
explanation: Saves customers both time and effort. People with very busy schedules are most likely to take advantage of this type of service. The technician can fix the computer at the customer's residence while the customer does other things at home. This saves the customer time because s/he does not need to disassemble the computer and take it to the repair shop. The amount of time it takes to work on the computer, the number of repairs that must be made to the computer, and the need to test the computer equipment is the same, regardless of where the repair is being made.

prompt: Rather than repositioning a product by changing its physical characteristics, price, or method of distribution, a technical business may decide to change the product's
explanation: Image. Changing image through promotional efforts is a common way to reposition products in the consumer's mind. Supply is a change in distribution. Profit is an element of price. Packaging is a physical characteristic.

prompt: An effective brand makes emotional and rational connections with customers primarily through
explanation: Touch points. Effective brands are built completely around the customer, with the customer perspective at the forefront of everything the business does. Effective brands build relationships with their customers by demonstrating brand values in every touch point, or connection, with customers. Employee input is valuable in brand development, but is not the primary way that brands connect with customers. Core values are what the business stands for, the "shoulds" that it will adhere to. Elements of a brand identity, (e.g., name, logo) simply represent the brand and what it stands for.

prompt: External factors that affect a cellular phone company's promotional decisions include
explanation: Competition and technology. The environment, social trends, and demand, in addition to competition and technology, are external factors, or influences from outside the cellular phone company, that have an effect on promotional decisions. Product, price, and distribution are internal factors.

prompt: What type of promotion does a technical company use to inform consumers about noncontroversial issues that are in the public's best interest?
explanation: Public service. Public-service promotions are a form of institutional promotion that are used to build goodwill for the technical company. Public-relations promotions deal with controversial issues that are in the public's best interest as well as being related in some way to the technical company or its products. Patronage promotions promote a technical company's prestige or its features. Product promotions are intended to stimulate sales.

prompt: Which of the following is an advantage of personal selling over advertising in the promotional mix:
explanation: Immediate feedback. In personal selling, the salesperson is able to learn immediately what the customer likes or dislikes about a product, whether the salesperson is helping the customer in person or over the telephone. This enables the salesperson to be flexible and to tailor the presentation to meet the needs of the particular customer. Personal selling is more costly on a per contact basis than advertising.

prompt: Which of the following broadcast media are growing at the fastest rate in terms of its use as an advertising medium:
explanation: Television. Due to increased interest in television (greater viewer time and more specialized stations), the use of this medium should continue to grow. Transit advertising is a form of promotion that is found in various modes of mass transportation (e.g., busses). Newspapers and direct mail are not forms of broadcast media.

prompt: Determine which of the following is a true statement about print ads:
choices: Advertisers must include the price of products in ads.
Advertisers like to use as much copy as possible.
Ad copy is intended to catch the reader's attention.
Ad copy can be any length that the advertiser wants.
explanation: Ad copy can be any length that the advertiser wants. The advertiser can use as much copy as s/he feels is needed to promote the product. This is usually limited also by the amount of money the advertiser wishes to spend. Advertisers do not use as much copy as possible, but use the amount of copy that they feel is appropriate to the product. There is no requirement that advertisers quote the price of their products, but many ads do include price. The headline rather than the copy is intended to catch the reader's attention.

prompt: A technical business planning a direct advertising campaign that targets professionals in a particular industry might consider purchasing a mailing list from a
explanation: Professional association. A professional association can be defined as a group of persons in the same industry who form a society with common interests and goals. Some trade associations sell their mailing lists to other businesses. For example, an electronics parts manufacturer might purchase a mailing list from a trade association that consists of members in the electronics industry. Trade industry is a general term used to describe businesses that buy and sell goods to others (e.g., retailers and wholesalers). Principal data source and resource investment agency are not terms commonly used to describe mailing list or database sources.

prompt: In developing sales material for technical selling, should you use a rational or emotional appeal?
choices: A combination of both. Some consumers will want the technical details of the products, while others will focus on how the product makes them feel.
Marketers have developed a specialized approach specifically for selling technical products that is neither rational nor emotional.
Emotional. Ultimately, consumers' purchase decisions for all products are made on the basis of how the products will make them feel.
Rational. For technical products, more than others, consumers concentrate solely on product specifications and descriptions.
explanation: A combination of both. Some consumers will want the technical details of the products, while others will focus on how the product makes them feel. A "combination" approach uses facts and logical reasoning (rational) that will appeal to some consumers, as well as appeals to aesthetics, ego, or feelings (emotional) that will attract others. Using strictly a rational approach in technical sales materials might make the products appear too dry and boring, even though some consumers would purchase on a rational basis anyway. Likewise, a strictly emotional approach, while appealing to consumers' feelings and aspirations, would bypass important factual aspects of the products. A specialized approach for technical products that is neither rational nor emotional is fictitious.

prompt: A local electronics store has set an amount to spend on advertising, established a promotional goal to increase sales, and scheduled its ads. The electronics store is engaged in creating a(n)
explanation: Promotional plan. A promotional plan is a guide for a local electronics store to follow in promoting the company and its goods and services. It includes an analysis of the electronics store's current situation, a description of the its promotional goals, the amount of money allocated to promotion, the promotional strategies and promotional mix the electronics store will use to achieve its promotional goals, and a timetable for the promotional plan. A marketing mix is the combination of the four elements of marketing—product, place, price, and promotion. An activity quota is a quota designed to control the ways that salespeople use their time and efforts. A balance sheet is a statement showing the financial status of the electronics.

prompt: Technical salespeople must be knowledgeable about products being promoted, and the technical business must have adequate stock of promoted items in order to coordinate __________ activities.
explanation: Promotional and selling. Failing to inform technical salespeople about promotions or failing to have adequate stock on hand can lead to dissatisfied customers and lost sales. Promotional and selling activities should be coordinated in order to increase sales. Promotional activities include advertising, visual merchandising, public relations, and publicity.

prompt: A computer company needs effective salespeople to build a loyal clientele. If the sales staff display inappropriate attitudes toward customers, the result is likely to be
explanation: High levels of customer turnover. Poor attitudes on the part of employees may lose customers for the computer company. More customers leave a computer company because of rude or indifferent treatment by employees than for any other reason. Salespeople with inappropriate attitudes receive little if any personal satisfaction from their work. The computer company is likely to have decreased profits and receive negative publicity.

prompt: Selling policies that are designed to govern the support a technical office equipment company provides customers after the sale are categorized as __________ policies.
explanation: Service. These policies can add to overall customer satisfaction, particularly when the technical product is complex, requires regular maintenance, or is new and attracts uncertain buyers who may later wish to return it. Return and adjustment, installation, and repair and maintenance are examples of service policies.

prompt: What is one way that electronics distributors use the technology of electronic data interchange in the selling function?
choices: To fax sales data to employees
explanation: To communicate with customers. An electronic data interchange (EDI) is a computerized information system. This technology allows an electronics distributor's computers to communicate with customers' (e.g., retail stores) computers and share information. An advantage of using EDI is that the computers keep track of sales and inventory and automatically place orders when inventory reaches a certain level. The system facilitates the sales process, which usually results in more satisfied customers and more sales for the business. Electronics distributors do not use electronic data interchange systems to identify potential accounts, fax sales data to employees, or access competitors' web sites.

prompt: In many technical businesses, the person who is the best internal source of product information for salespeople is the
explanation: Buyer. Buyers are expected to know technical products they purchase "inside and out." It is often part of a buyer's responsibilities to provide salespersons with product information to help them with their selling. The inventory manager is responsible for the stock that a technical business has on hand. Customers are often good sources of product information, but they are external rather than internal sources. The accountant handles financial record keeping for the technical business.

prompt: A computer manufacturer's catalogs, manuals, and print advertisements are a good source of __________ information for salespeople.
explanation: Product. A great deal of product information is given in product bulletins, catalogs, manuals, and print advertisements. Salespeople who read these materials usually are able to obtain information that will help them sell computer products to customers. A computer manufacturer's catalog provides information that customers may use to order products. Some manuals contain information about operating policies and procedures. Print advertisements are a type of promotion.

prompt: After learning that a customer is interested in a computer that can produce sophisticated graphics, what should be the salesperson's next step?
choices: Trying to make the customer feel more relaxed
Trying to reach closure with the customer
Suggesting a specific computer to the customer
Giving the customer a price list
explanation: Suggesting a specific computer to the customer. After learning about the customer's needs, the next step is to prescribe a solution (specific computer). The salesperson should be well informed about the products s/he sells in order to suggest the most appropriate product. Price should be discussed as part of prescribing a solution to the customer's need, but giving the customer a price list at this point would disrupt the selling process. Making the customer feel relaxed and at ease is part of establishing a relationship with the customer. The salesperson should not try to reach closure before a suitable product has been recommended and demonstrated.

prompt: Scott, a sales associate at Stereo Sounds, shows a customer two different stereo systems. The customer asks Scott, "How do the speakers on the 200 model compare to the speakers on the 350 model?" Scott is dealing with what type of customer personality?
explanation: Fact-finder. This type of personality is characterized by a customer expecting the salesperson to be knowledgeable about the products and be able to present the facts. Fact-finders prefer to comparison shop, like to see variety, and want specific information. An informed personality is a basic type of customer personality characterized by the customer's display of confidence in choices, spending for quality, being a trendsetter, and/or wanting the best. A decisive personality is a basic type of customer personality characterized by the customer's asking for specific items, having a businesslike nature, acting in a direct manner, knowing what s/he wants, and/or shopping quickly. A difficult personality is a basic type of customer personality; these types of customers have problems that interfere with their ability to communicate satisfactorily or to function in a normal or pleasant manner. They may be disagreeable, domineering, suspicious, slow, or dishonest.

prompt: Pausing is a very effective questioning technique because it gives the
choices: salesperson a chance to greet other customers.
salesperson a chance to total the sales.
customer an opportunity to close the sale.
customer an opportunity to ask questions.
explanation: Customer an opportunity to ask questions. Other benefits of pausing are to relax the pace of the sale, to give salespersons a chance to plan what they should say, and to give the customer a chance to absorb all the information. The amount of the total sale will be calculated at the close, which is handled by the salesperson, not the customer. Pausing might create an opportunity to greet other customers, but that is not its purpose.

prompt: Which of the following situations would probably require the most in-depth probing by a salesperson:
choices: The customer is buying copier paper.
The customer is buying AA batteries.
The customer is buying a digital camera.
explanation: The customer is buying a digital camera. More probing will probably be used when expensive, sophisticated products are being sold rather than inexpensive, easy-to-operate ones. Although probing can be used in the other selling situations, it probably will not be as in-depth as for a digital camera.

prompt: When technical salespeople recommend an appropriate substitute product, one of the benefits to the customer is that the customer often
explanation: Saves time. By recommending appropriate substitute products, technical salespeople often help customers save time and the inconvenience of going from business to business in order to locate a specific product. Customers appreciate being told of substitute products that will provide as much, or even more, satisfaction than the item they originally requested. Substitute products are not necessarily less expensive than the items that they originally requested. Not all products include a rebate. In some cases, the substitute product might be priced the same as the original product. However, in most cases it is either priced higher or lower. It is a benefit to the customer if the product is lower priced rather than the same price.

prompt: A point of difference between a customer and a salesperson that may prevent the sale of a computer is a(n)
explanation: Objection. An objection is the customer's reason for not buying the computer. It should be viewed as an opportunity rather than an obstacle for the salesperson. An excuse is an insincere statement used to conceal the real reason for not buying the computer. Inquiry and testimonial are methods of handling objections. The inquiry method reveals the customer's needs through careful questioning. The testimonial method refutes objections by citing the experiences of other purchasers of the good/service.

prompt: It is a good idea for photocopier salespeople to practice operating the photocopiers and explaining their features in order to __________ them effectively.
explanation: Demonstrate. Practicing how to operate a photocopier will help the photocopier salesperson conduct an effective demonstration. A photocopier salesperson who is unfamiliar with a photocopier's functions and features may be embarrassed if s/he cannot make the photocopier perform as expected during a sales presentation. Practicing will help work out any "bugs" that might occur during the demonstration. A photocopier salesperson is not responsible for installing, repairing, or servicing products.

prompt: After the customer has made a decision to buy a computer, the salesperson may be able to increase the amount of the sale by using
explanation: Suggestion selling. This is a sales technique in which the salesperson attempts to increase the customer's computer purchase by suggesting additional items (e.g., printers, scanners) after the original decision to buy has been made. The suggestion of additional items should be made before the original sale is completed. Substitute selling is offering an alternative to the customer when the originally requested merchandise is unavailable or will not meet the customer's real needs. A silence close is a closing technique in which the salesperson stops talking after the presentation to allow the prospect time to think and to respond. A sales incentive is a reward to the salesperson for making sales.

prompt: In order to effectively sell a computer printer to an individual, what should a salesperson do after recognizing that the individual has a need?
explanation: Provide information. To effectively sell a computer printer, salespeople should provide the information about the printer that will satisfy the individual's needs. If individuals already know what they need, the salesperson may only need to show them the printer and answer a few simple questions. However, if the individuals are not sure about what they want, a salesperson may need to provide a lot of information about price, benefits, uses, warranties, etc. Providing the right information will help make the sale. Only when individuals have all the information they need, will the salesperson be able to sell a computer printer. After an individual decides to buy a computer printer, a salesperson might offer to arrange financing. Brochures may be used to provide information, but they are prepared in advance.

prompt: What information should technical office equipment salespeople include in a written sales proposal for a group presentation?
choices: Product pricing and benefits for each item presented
An outline addressing the primary decision maker's questions
Data addressing each group member's specific needs and concerns
The presenter's qualifications and credentials to establish credibility
explanation: Data addressing each group member's specific needs and concerns. Before sales proposals can be distributed at a group sales presentation, technical office equipment salespeople need to research how the technical product(s) can benefit all members of the group. It is possible that each group member has different needs or concerns. Therefore, before presentations are assembled, technical office equipment salespeople must probe each group member before recommending or proposing solutions. By addressing only the primary decision maker's questions, the technical office equipment salespeople risk alienating other group members who might influence the key decision maker's opinion. Although it helps for technical office equipment salespeople to present their qualifications to establish credibility, it does not necessarily need to be presented in a written sales proposal.

prompt: An electronics store's employees receive a 20% discount on all purchases. What is the amount of an employee's discount on the purchase of a $35.00 calculator and a $12.00 rechargable battery?
explanation: $9.40. The combined purchase is $47.00 ($35 + $12 = $47). The 20% discount is calculated on the total amount of the purchase ($47.00 x .20 = $9.40).

prompt: Information that the cellular phone salesperson needs when deciding if a lead is a prospect, is whether the lead has
explanation: The authority to purchase. Leads cannot be considered prospects unless they have been qualified, which includes determining whether they have the authority to purchase. Determining whether the lead has heard of the cellular phone salesperson's product or is in a convenient location would not be part of qualifying a lead. Whether the lead has been qualified by competing cellular phone salespersons is information that would probably not be available.

prompt: Cable service companies often conclude sales letters by asking customers to
explanation: Take action. Sales letters usually ask customers to do something such as place an order, make a phone call, or fill out and return an enclosed card. A cable service company often asks customers to take action in the last paragraph of the sales letter. The main part of the sales letter explains and informs, while the last paragraph is a call to action, which is signing up for a specific cable service. After reading the first part of the letter, customers will understand the value of taking the requested action. Social letters are used to invite customers to open houses. Sales letters usually do not ask customers to donate money or make referrals.

prompt: Recognition awards should be used
explanation: With other incentives. Recognition awards can be effective motivators, but they are not strong motivators. They need to be used with other incentives for strong, continued effectiveness.

prompt: One advantage for technical sales representatives who follow a sales-call schedule is that it
choices: keeps them organized and might reduce travel time.
keeps them organized and decreases sales profitability.
reduces travel time and requires less customer follow-up.
requires less customer follow-up and increases travel expenses.
explanation: Keeps them organized and might reduce travel time. Although many factors are considered when developing a sales-call pattern (e.g., customer size, sales volume, customer proximity), one advantage is that it keeps the sales representatives organized. They know where and when they are visiting particular customers and can prepare for any presentations or demonstrations that might fit each customer's needs or wants. It can also reduce travel time, if the sales calls are made to customers that are located in the same area. A sales-call schedule does not necessarily reduce the need for customer follow-up, increase travel expenses, or decrease sales profitability.

prompt: The most important factors to consider in planning a route for a technical company's sales force are
choices: travel maximization and minimization of selling time.
number and distribution of customers in territory.
geographic size and shape of the sales territory.
explanation: Geographic size and shape of the sales territory. This is most important since it will allow maximum selling time and minimum travel time. Number and distribution of customers is the next consideration, followed by sales-call frequency and duration. Non-selling time should be minimized and selling time maximized.

prompt: What is the primary factor technical sales managers consider when assigning territories to sales representatives?
choices: The representative's selling skills and abilities
The level of sales training offered by the company
The number of previous jobs each representative has held
explanation: The representative's selling skills and abilities. Each person has unique strengths and weaknesses that should be considered when assigning sales territories. Some salespeople are more aggressive in trying to get new accounts, while others are better at working with existing accounts. Since the sales manager's goal is to maximize sales, it is best to give an aggressive sales representative a less-developed area. Although previous selling experience might affect the territory assignments, the number of previous jobs that each representative has had is not a factor. Generally, sales training programs are completed before a representative starts the daily task of selling; the program and degree of training is the same for each representative because they all go through the same program. Therefore, the company's level of sales training is not a primary factor. In ethical terms, a sales manager should base territory assignments on what is best for the company and the representative, not personal preferences.

prompt: Before establishing prospecting standards, technical sales managers often develop a
explanation: Market analysis. To increase sales, technical companies first need to evaluate how their products are currently being used and where the products have potential use. By conducting a study or analyzing different market segments, technical sales managers can identify new target markets for their products. Once the markets are determined, sales managers can use the information to establish appropriate criteria to qualify prospects. A customer profile is maintained by sales representatives and documents detailed information including contacts, key decision makers, and sales history. A sales report is a summary of various sales information and is collected for many purposes. For example, sales reports are often used to flag slow-moving products or a salesperson's activities. Cold calls are unannounced visits by a salesperson to prospects about whom little may be known. A cold-call summary is a report that records a salesperson's activities in regard to cold calling.

prompt: Kathy has just been asked to redesign the sales training program for Edgar's Electronics Company. She will need to analyze the company's needs and
choices: create training goals structured around corporate mandates.
set training objectives which are realistic, specific, and measurable.
plan group instruction so that large numbers of people can benefit.
base the training efforts on sales formulas and memorization.
explanation: Set training objectives which are realistic, specific, and measurable. Goals must be attainable during the allocated training time and should use the financial resources available. They should be geared to the attitudes, knowledge, and skills of those in the training program, not according to corporate mandates. Training must be planned for both individual and group instruction. Training should be challenging and not dependent on rote memorization.

prompt: A cost-effective way for a computer software company to train sales personnel to use its new products is to develop a training program that uses
explanation: Interactive multimedia. Interactive multimedia is an extremely cost-effective method of training. This type of training implements self-guided, computer-based instruction. It can be done anytime, anywhere, and is less expensive than hiring instructors. Role-playing techniques are appropriate when training in areas of customer or interpersonal relationships. Classroom and lecture methods require instructors. Lectures are better in some training situations, but learning computer software products requires hands-on experience. Individual instruction is a more expensive training method.

prompt: A large corporation that sells several lines of diverse technical goods might manage its sales staff by implementing a ___________ organizational structure.
explanation: Product specialization. As a result of mergers and consolidations, some companies have become very large and diversified in nature. For example, a large electronics company might sell calculators, electronic scales, and automated machinery. All items are used by different markets for different purposes. Therefore, some companies opt to organize their sales staff to specialize in certain product lines. The advantage in creating a specialized selling team is that sales personnel are generally well educated about a specific product. In the eyes of the customer, the salesperson has credibility and exercises expertise in relation to a narrow scope of products. Pure-line organization refers to a structure in which decision making is done by one person. Small companies are often organized in this manner. Multilevel marketing is a business structure that pays commission on sales earned by people at two or more levels; the sales representatives usually work independent of the company; and the representatives not only sell products but try to get others to sell them. Cross-function organizations are generally short-term in nature. Members are gathered to complete a task or objective and then disband once the task has been completed.

prompt: What is a popular "extra" term that a sales manager may encourage the technical sales force to use to close the sale?
choices: Discounts, since price will always be the most important term
Rebates, because customers most like getting money back
Additional time allotted to make payments
"Value-added" components, such as information or service
explanation: "Value added" components, such as information or service. Technical sales managers encourage their sales force to make the terms of the sale as attractive as possible to customers, within the boundaries of profitability and general company policy. With technical companies finding it more difficult to offer competitive advantages or unique terms to their customers, a sales manager will encourage salespeople to include "value-added" components to the terms of the sale. These are items offered at no additional cost to the customer, which enhance the product. Information and service are two of the most popular. Discounts are appealing, and price is important, but may hurt profitability or be matched by competitors. Likewise, including additional time to make payments can be attractive, but can easily be matched by competitors. Rebates, too, can be an attractive term of the sale, but do not provide the longer-term value inherent in a value-added term, such as information or service.
